problem.title: One Team, Two Orders
problem.statement: Ava, Ben, and Cleo are available. Two different people are chosen to form one team, and the team has no special roles. How many different teams are possible?
hints: Do Ava-Ben and Ben-Ava form different teams?

solutionSteps.title: Count ordered descriptions
solutionSteps.body: There are 3 choices for the first name and 2 remaining choices for the second, giving 3 × 2 = 6 ordered descriptions.

solutionSteps.title: Group descriptions of the same team
solutionSteps.body: Ava-Ben and Ben-Ava name the same team. The same is true for Ava-Cleo and Cleo-Ava, and for Ben-Cleo and Cleo-Ben.

solutionSteps.title: Remove the equal duplication
solutionSteps.body: Each actual team appears in exactly 2 ordered descriptions, so 6 ÷ 2 = 3 teams.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of the three unordered teams
notes: The teams are Ava-Ben, Ava-Cleo, and Ben-Cleo.
The no-roles condition makes reversed name orders descriptions of one outcome, not different outcomes.

problem.title: Beacon Cords
problem.statement: Five labeled beacons stand in a field. One cord is stretched between every pair of beacons. How many cords are used?
hints: Count a direction from one endpoint to another first.
How many times does the same cord appear in that directed count?

solutionSteps.title: Count directed descriptions
solutionSteps.body: Choose a starting beacon in 5 ways and a different ending beacon in 4 ways, giving 5 × 4 = 20 directed descriptions.

solutionSteps.title: Pair the reversals
solutionSteps.body: The descriptions A→B and B→A refer to the same physical cord. Every cord has exactly two endpoints, so every cord appears exactly twice.

solutionSteps.title: Correct the count
solutionSteps.body: Dividing the 20 descriptions by the uniform multiplicity 2 gives 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cords.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of the ten unordered beacon pairs

problem.title: Festival Duets
problem.statement: Six musicians attend a festival. Each possible two-person duet performs once. How many duet performances are there?
hints: A first-name, second-name list has 6 × 5 entries.
Does reversing the names create a new duet?

solutionSteps.title: Build an ordered list
solutionSteps.body: There are 6 choices for the first listed musician and 5 for the second, giving 30 ordered name lists.

solutionSteps.title: Check the multiplicity
solutionSteps.body: For every duet, the two name orders describe the same performers. No duet has more or fewer than these two descriptions.

solutionSteps.title: Divide once
solutionSteps.body: The 30 ordered descriptions form pairs, so there are 30 ÷ 2 = 15 duet performances.

problem.title: Two Identical Flags
problem.statement: Five flags are arranged in a row. Two flags are identical red flags; the other three are distinct blue, green, and yellow flags. How many visibly different rows are possible?
hints: Temporarily label the red flags R₁ and R₂.
How many labeled rows collapse to each visible row?

solutionSteps.title: Temporarily distinguish the flags
solutionSteps.body: If the red flags are labeled R₁ and R₂, all 5 flags are distinct and can be arranged in 5! = 120 rows.

solutionSteps.title: Find the duplicate descriptions
solutionSteps.body: Swapping R₁ and R₂ changes the labeled row but not the visible color row. Every visible row has exactly these two labeled descriptions.

solutionSteps.title: Remove the labels
solutionSteps.body: Because the multiplicity is uniformly 2, the number of visible rows is 120 ÷ 2 = 60.

validationMethods: enumeration of 120 labeled permutations followed by erasing red subscripts
independent choice of two red positions times 3! orders of the other flags: 10×6
notes: Both methods give 60 visibly different rows.

problem.title: Two-Scoop Cups
problem.statement: An ice cream shop has four flavors. A cup gets two scoops, flavors may repeat, and top-versus-bottom order does not matter. How many different flavor selections are possible?
hints: The 4 × 4 ordered scoop list has both mixed cups and double-flavor cups.
Do those two kinds have the same number of ordered descriptions?

solutionSteps.title: Separate the unequal multiplicities
solutionSteps.body: There are 4 double-flavor cups. Each, such as vanilla-vanilla, has only one ordered description.

solutionSteps.title: Pair the mixed descriptions
solutionSteps.body: The ordered grid has 12 mixed-flavor descriptions. Reversing the two flavors pairs them uniformly, giving 12 ÷ 2 = 6 mixed selections.

solutionSteps.title: Combine the two kinds
solutionSteps.body: The total is 4 double-flavor selections plus 6 mixed selections, or 10. Dividing all 16 descriptions by 2 would fail because the multiplicity is not uniform.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of the ten unordered flavor multisets
independent split into 4 repeated-flavor selections and 12÷2 mixed selections
notes: The four diagonal ordered pairs have multiplicity one; the six off-diagonal orbits have multiplicity two.
